title: Claude Code / Tradovate / Automated MNQ Trading
author: RickSmith3821
selftext:
I've had Claude Code hooked upo to robinhood MCP since June 26.   That was useless because I trade futures and Robinhood hasn't yet allowed MCP's to trade futures.   Pivoted, and now I'm using Claude Code / Python scanner (bridge) with Tradingview (Claude extension in a browser to get the real time futures quotes) / [Pickmytrade.trade](http://Pickmytrade.trade) to send a JSON signal to via webhook and then on to Tradovate through that to make the trade. Been running this in simulation mode, and it's been "OK" at best, mostly garbage.

I asked Claude the other day ... "If you can run in the browser to use tradingview to GET the symbol info, why can't you just make the trades in tradovate ?"

Answer: "Because I'm not allowed under any circumstances to touch financial transactions."

I'm getting sick of these AI attitudes.

So I had Claude build me a completely independent Python system that does (most of) everything. Like I said, I had to give up control of a browser extension for Claude to be able to get real-time quotes for MNQ ... that stuff's just not available anywhere that I know of without paying real money for it.

The method ?   I'm making trades on the 1m MNQ. JUST lookin for 2 red candles, a green and then going long until I see a red.

Rules ?   Here's Claudes summary of the current ruleset;

  Entry: long only

  \- Signal: two red 1m candles, then a green candle. It buys 7 MNQ at the green candle's close.

  \- Shorts: off. The 3-green-then-2-red short pattern is built but disabled.

  \- All entry filters are off:

\- EMA200 trend filter: off

\- Chop filter (efficiency ratio): off. It's set to 0.15, not the 0.30 that won the replay, so check that if you turn it back on.

\- Bar-range filter (skip when the 10-bar average range is over 15 pts): off

  \- Re-entry cooldown: 90s after an exit. On 1m bars this skips the bar right after an exit.



Exits

  \- Initial stop: 30 pts below entry. The comments still describe an 18-pt stop, but the live value is 30.

  \- Trailing stop: 25 pts behind the highest price since entry, starting on the first bar. The stop only moves up, and it fills at the stop price if a bar's low touches it.

  \- NO\_CONFIRM: on. If either of the first two bars after entry closes red, it exits at that bar's close.

  \- No profit target.

  \- Session close: open positions are closed and no new entries are taken from 16:00 to 18:00 daily, and from Friday 16:00 to Sunday 18:00.

  \- Manual exit: posting EXIT in Discord (from your user ID) closes the position right away.



Plumbing

  \- Data comes from TradingView MNQ1! 1m bars, including overnight, checked every 30s (not synced to bar close).

  \- Orders go through PickMyTrade to your Tradovate demo account: 7× MNQZ6 under the strategy name "RedFlip".

  \- Entries and exits are posted to Discord.

  
  
Oh.. some real time results. Last week.

Sunday -> Monday - $3,550

Monday -> Tuesday - $250

Tuesday -> Wednesday - ( $1,850 )

Wednesday -> Thursday - ( $750 )

Thursday -> Friday - ( $1,550 )

So a loss for the week. ALL weeks have been like this... a big winner somewhere, but then dribbling off the profits...

  
I'd be interested to hear feedback on this method, or hear what other people are doing mechanically... DM me if need be.

Thanks for this community!  It should pay off for all of us !  Let's get it before the bots cut us off.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
Five days isn't enough to say much either way, but the pattern you describe (one big day, then it dribbles back) is what a trailing-stop system with no real entry edge tends to look like. The first thing I'd do is run the same exits on random entries: same 30-point stop, same 25-point trail, same NO\_CONFIRM rule, but entering at random times. If that looks similar, the "two red then green" signal isn't doing much and the exit rules are producing the equity curve. On 1-minute MNQ that pattern is close to noise by itself.

Also check how much of the P&L comes from a few event days. Your Sunday to Monday win of $3,550 looks like the kind of move that happens on a big macro release or a gap. If most of the profit is one or two days like that and the rest is small losses, the strategy is really a bet on volatility spikes. Cymetica's EventTrader has pre-tagged event timing (CPI, FOMC, NFP and so on), so you could tag each trade and see how it does on event days versus quiet ones, and whether standing down around releases would save the dribble.

Simulation results deserve caution too. Sim fills at the bar close or at the exact stop price are optimistic, especially with the 30-second polling not synced to the bar. On MNQ, real stops slip, and seven contracts plus commissions adds up over hundreds of trades. I'd want the trade count, average win, average loss and net expectancy after costs before drawing any conclusion.

The filters that "won the replay" are worth a second look as well. If you tuned them on the same data, that's the part most likely to be overfit. What was the trade count behind that replay?

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body:
You’re actually further along than you probably think. Since you already have an independent Python execution system, I wouldn’t spend too much time changing the plumbing now. I’d focus on proving or disproving the strategy itself.

Build a clean backtest that reproduces the bot’s rules as closely as possible — same entry timing, stop, trailing logic, session restrictions, cooldowns and ideally realistic fees/slippage.

At the same time, keep running it on a demo account for 30 days under conditions as close to live trading as possible. Then compare the demo trades against the backtest trade by trade, not just total P&L. If they don’t match, find out why before optimizing anything.

The most useful thing we found when developing our own system was to stop asking AI to “improve the strategy” and instead use it to analyse the losing periods. Find the worst drawdowns, go back to those exact market conditions and look for what they had in common. Then change **one thing at a time**, backtest again and repeat.

With your current rules I’d especially look at whether those big winning days are being given back during chop or regime changes. Since most of your filters are currently off, you should be able to test that quite cleanly.

AI is very useful for building the framework and analysing the data, but I wouldn’t let it blindly optimise parameters for the highest backtest result. That’s an easy way to overfit.

It’s a lot of work, but after a month of synchronized demo + backtest data you’ll know much more than you do now.

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
Before changing the pattern, I’d verify that RedFlip acts only on finalized candles. Polling MNQ1! every 30 seconds means a currently green 1m bar can turn red before close, and two polls could observe the same qualifying bar unless signals are keyed to its timestamp. The screenshot’s “<200ms execution” claim for PickMyTrade does not fix either issue.

Also, signals come from continuous MNQ1! while orders target MNQZ6. Around rollover, their prices and volume behavior can diverge. Does each Discord entry record the three completed bar timestamps, observed prices, contract mapping, webhook ID, and Tradovate fill? That trace would show whether the weekly loss comes from the rule or from bar-state and routing mismatches.
